question: Why did treating wild wombats for mange need a drug that stays in the body for weeks?
answer: Because a wild wombat can rarely be dosed twice. Ivermectin and moxidectin are short-acting, so one dose often fails to kill every mite and weekly repeats are needed. Fluralaner, sold as a dog flea treatment, lingers for weeks; in a small trial one dose cleared mange in wild wombats within three to four weeks.
move: Choose the remedy that works on the only chance you will get.
